In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virus is not excluded by the nuclear membrane during the mitotic process, but that it is not included in the nuclear membrane during telophase.
the virus is excluded from the nucleus of infected cells during cell division.
the tobacco mosaic virus does not enter the nucleus, but is associated with the chromosomes and is left outside the nuclear envelopes during the formation of new nuclei in mitosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
virus particles and aggregates of particles are excluded from the daughter nuclei, but that the virus is not eliminated from dividing mesophyll of the infected leaf.
tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus that is non-enveloped and rod-shaped.
the virus does not appear to interfere with the division of the mesophyll cells, but that the nuclear envelope is a permeable barrier to the virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tobacco mosaic virus can replicate in dividing cells.
tobacco plants are able to produce a high amount of TMV particles in a short time.
we can use the same tools and approaches to investigate plant viruses as we would for animal viruses.
